From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery — infra gating questions and next steps

Hi Nora / Ravi — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the gating items that will drive whether Medico should go Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or a Private VPC/on-prem deployment:

1) Primary constraints raised on the call:
- SSO: SAML 2.0 IdP with SCIM provisioning required for staff provisioning (Okta).
- Key management: BYOK requirement; HSM-backed keys preferred for primary encryption of model artifacts and KV store.
- Logging & retention: audit logs and request/response traces must be retained for 7 years for compliance.
- Data residency: production data must live in us-east-1.
- PHI: end-to-end controls required for PHI processing (Business Associate Agreement).

2) How these map to deployment decisions:
- Hosted API: fastest, but will require carve-outs for BYOK/HSM and long-term log retention — typically not a fit when HSM + 7-year retention is mandatory.
- Dedicated: provides reserved capacity + stronger isolation and can support customer-managed KMS integrations; limited HSM options (we use a KMS proxy model).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control for VPC peering, HSM integration, and long retention windows — usually the safest path for regulated PHI workloads.

3) Immediate asks / proposed next steps:
- Nora: please confirm the absolute must-haves vs nice-to-haves (HSM yes/no; 7-year retention hard requirement?).
- We will deliver a short tech checklist (size + network + KMS) and a pricing delta between Dedicated and Private by EOD Monday.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive (Priyom + infra) next week to validate integration points (VPC, KMS, log export).

I attached the RFI workbook and a one-pager that outlines Dedicated vs Private trade-offs. If anything above is inaccurate, flag it and I’ll update.

Thanks,
Vivek
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- HSM: preferred and likely mandatory for production PHI; we are currently evaluating Thales vs AWS CloudHSM. If Dedicated cannot support HSM-backed BYOK we will need Private.
- Log retention: 7 years is a hard requirement for certain audit trails (access logs + request metadata). We cannot truncate them to 90 days.
- SSO: Okta SAML + SCIM are non-negotiable for provisioning.
- Timeline: procurement is targetting end of Q2. We need high-level cost delta ASAP to size the budget.

Next steps: please route the tech checklist to our infra lead (Ravi) and include any specifics on network topologies you support for Private (peering, transit, on-prem VPN). We can block time for a deep dive Tue/Wed next week (PST).

Priyom's notes:
- Hosted API: supports customer SAML/SCIM for user-facing admin, but BYOK/HSM and 7-year log retention are operationally challenging on shared hosted infrastructure. We can offer envelope encryption with customer KMS for some artifacts, but not HSM-backed key material for the runtime.
- Dedicated: can integrate with customer-managed KMS via a KMS proxy or customer VPN to a KMS endpoint; log forwarding to customer-managed SIEM is supported but retention beyond our standard window requires legal/contract amendment + additional storage fees. HSM integration is limited and depends on the provider; we typically recommend Private for mandatory HSM.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): supports direct HSM attachments (customer or cloud HSM), full control over log retention (we can ship logs to your S3/obj store in your account and you control lifecycle policies), and strict VPC isolation.

Action items for deep-dive:
- Bring network diagrams (Ravi) and KMS/HSM vendor preferences.
- Priyom to draft a short architecture doc outlining the KMS proxy model vs Private HSM flow.
- Vivek to prepare a high-level cost delta (Dedicated vs Private) and share procurement checklist.
